T1.implementation_approach: Use a component-based design approach with a framework like React or Vue.js. Create reusable components for problem cards, filters, and search functionality.
T1.notes: Focus on responsive design and user-friendly navigation.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs using a framework like Express.js or Django. Implement endpoints for CRUD operations on problems.
T2.notes: Ensure proper error handling and input validation.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a relational database schema with tables for problems, categories, and tags. Use an ORM like Sequelize or SQLAlchemy for database interactions.
T3.notes: Optimize schema for search and filtering.

T4.implementation_approach: Use Axios or Fetch API to connect the frontend with backend APIs. Implement state management for seamless data flow.
T4.notes: Handle loading states and error messages effectively.

T5.implementation_approach: Design a code editor using libraries like Monaco Editor or CodeMirror. Add syntax highlighting, line numbers, and theme support.
T5.notes: Ensure the editor is responsive and supports multiple languages.

T6.implementation_approach: Develop an API to execute code using a sandbox environment. Use Docker or similar tools to isolate execution.
T6.notes: Ensure security by sandboxing code execution.

T7.implementation_approach: Set up a containerized environment using Docker to support multiple programming languages. Pre-install necessary compilers and interpreters.

T8.implementation_approach: Connect the code editor UI with the backend execution API. Use WebSocket for real-time updates.
T8.notes: Provide real-time feedback for code execution.

T9.implementation_approach: Implement logic to compare user-submitted code output with expected output. Use a scoring system for evaluation.
T9.notes: Handle edge cases and provide detailed feedback.

T10.implementation_approach: Design a user profile page with sections for user details, activity history, and achievements. Use a responsive design framework.
T10.notes: Focus on a clean and intuitive layout.

T11.implementation_approach: Develop APIs for user profile management, including endpoints for fetching and updating user data.
T11.notes: Ensure secure handling of user data.

T12.implementation_approach: Design a database schema for user profiles, including tables for user details, activity logs, and achievements.
T12.notes: Optimize for quick retrieval of user data.

T13.implementation_approach: Use Axios or Fetch API to connect the user profile UI with backend APIs. Implement state management for seamless data flow.

T14.implementation_approach: Design a leaderboard UI with sortable columns for rank, user, and score. Use a responsive design framework.
T14.notes: Ensure the leaderboard is visually appealing and easy to navigate.

T15.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to fetch leaderboard data. Implement logic to calculate rankings based on user scores.

T16.implementation_approach: Design a database schema for leaderboard data, including tables for user scores and rankings.
T16.notes: Ensure schema supports efficient sorting and filtering.

T17.implementation_approach: Use Axios or Fetch API to connect the leaderboard UI with backend APIs. Implement real-time updates using WebSocket.

T18.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests for the problem library functionality. Use tools like Jest or Mocha.
T18.notes: Focus on edge cases and performance testing.

T19.implementation_approach: Test the code editor and execution backend using automated and manual testing. Validate syntax highlighting and execution results.
T19.notes: Ensure security and performance under load.

T20.implementation_approach: Test user profile functionality, including data retrieval and updates. Use tools like Postman for API testing.
T20.notes: Focus on data consistency and security.

T21.implementation_approach: Test leaderboard functionality, including data fetching and sorting. Use automated tests for performance validation.
T21.notes: Ensure accurate ranking and real-time updates.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize SQLAlchemy instance
db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Problem {self.id}: {self.title}>'

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    status = db.Column(db.String(20), nullable=False, default='Pending')
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    user = db.relationship('User', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

    def __init__(self, user_id, problem_id, code, language, status='Pending'):
        self.user_id = user_id
        self.problem_id = problem_id
        self.code = code
        self.language = language
        self.status = status

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Solution id={self.id} user_id={self.user_id} problem_id={self.problem_id} status={self.status}>"

# app/routes.py
# Module: app.routes
# Layer: assembly

from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

def register_blueprints(app):
    """
    Register all blueprints to the Flask application instance.

    Args:
        app (Flask): The Flask application instance.
    """
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint, url_prefix='/problems')
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint, url_prefix='/users')
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint, url_prefix='/solutions')

from flask import Flask
from app.routes import problem_blueprint, user_blueprint, solution_blueprint

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    
    # Register blueprints
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint)
    
    return app

from app import create_app

# Entry point for the application
if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = create_app()
    app.run(debug=True)

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style competitive programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Editor: An integrated code editor with support for multiple programming languages.
- Online Judge: An automated system to evaluate and provide feedback on submitted solutions.
- User Profiles: Profiles for users to track their progress, achievements, and rankings.
- Leaderboard: A leaderboard to display top-performing users based on problem-solving performance.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
